description: Multi-phase plans currently in flight. Each phase references roadmap item ids; the activePhase section breaks the current phase into concrete tasks with status. Survives conversation compactions — a fresh session can pick up by reading this file.

phases.title: Foundation
phases.notes: Schema, bus, episodic memory, agent base. Nothing alive yet — just the substrate everything else hangs off.

phases.title: First Voice
phases.notes: Cheshire Cat end-to-end. Talking to himself. Layered context composer + engagement policy + ADR writer come online here because the Cat is their first consumer.

phases.title: First Tension
phases.notes: Add the White Rabbit. Two voices, role tension, semantic + relational memory layers populated as the agents accumulate history. Compaction-as-behavior arrives because it has to.

phases.title: First Race
phases.notes: Dodo orchestrator + quiescence + conflict resolution + first showcase (/health endpoint). The system runs end-to-end on a trivial directive. Init CLI lands here so the showcase can run against a real target project.

phases.title: Full Cast
phases.notes: Bring the rest of the cast online with integration tests per agent. Per-character artifact handlers for the new speech act payloads. Synthetic-consensus guard goes here because it only matters once disagreement is real.

phases.title: Real Threads
phases.notes: The hard showcases — translation chat MVP, security recovery, multi-session persistence. Transcript annotation tooling lets us publish them. Token telemetry confirms the engagement_policy is paying for itself. Closed out 2026-05-08; substrate-convergence work in analyses 026-030 + the Geocities showcase landed the "Tweedles don't ship" bug class. P7 evals deferred behind P8 (operator interface) so the eval harness has a usable surface to run against.

phases.title: Observer API
phases.notes: HistoricalRunHandle reads any captured snapshot directory — parses run.log, reads the per-agent SQLite databases, loads the telemetry JSON, exposes summary() / meetings() / utterances() / per_agent_telemetry() / artifacts(). The replay-side surface that everything else in P8 sits on. Shipped 2026-05-07 alongside P8.2.

phases.title: TUI Inspector
phases.notes: Textual-based read-only TUI: snapshot library, run summary, meeting detail with body preview + speaker filter + utterance modal, artifact browser (global + meeting-scoped, attribution via bus not mtime), cast view, theme cycling, app-wide vim navigation. First public release — wonderland-ai 0.0.1 on PyPI 2026-05-08.

phases.title: Streaming + Mock Turtle
phases.notes: Foundation for live-watch UX. Extend RunHandle with stream_events() async iterator; HistoricalRunHandle defaults to yield-now (no behavior change for inspector); MockTurtleHandle replays a snapshot's events with compressed timing + dwell cap so we iterate live-watch UI against a free testbed. After P8.3 the TUI can subscribe to "events as they arrive" without caring whether the source is replay, mock, or eventually a real bus.

phases.title: Live-watch screen
phases.notes: New LiveRunScreen that consumes the streaming API — meeting cells fill in as events arrive, current speaker indicator, live cost ticker, drill-down into in-progress meetings shows partial transcripts. Iterated entirely against Mock Turtle replay so zero API spend during UX iteration. The screen that turns Wonderland from "things happen and you read transcripts later" into "things happen and you watch them happen."

phases.title: Directive issuing + LiveRunHandle
phases.notes: NewRunScreen — directive textarea, workflow picker (TDD/canonical/smoke), project-root picker. LiveRunHandle wraps a real Runner+Caucus, emits via the same streaming API as MockTurtleHandle so the live-watch screen consumes both interchangeably. The leap from "replay testbed" to "actually launches a real run." First end-to-end test: directive → live watch → artifacts → done.

phases.title: New-project spinup (the rabbit hole)
phases.notes: Three entry paths converging on a single project-context capture: greenfield (skeleton picker + scaffold), existing-Wonderland (already covered by P8.5's project picker), adopt-existing (wonderland init + stack-detection routine that pre-fills the context form from manifest files). Persists .wonderland/project-context.md in a forward-compatible shape so future workflow-context injection has one input format to read. The on-ramp that turns "pip install" into "team's ready to start."

phases.title: First-use polish
phases.notes: Welcome/home screen (new run / browse snapshots / cast / configure), error states (missing API key, no project root, run failure), abort flow (clean shutdown of running threads), quiescence indicator (M5's long pauses need "still working, just thinking"), README + SHOWCASE updates with the TUI flow. The rough-edges sweep that closes the gap between "works for the developer" and "works for someone who just installed it."

phases.title: Evals
phases.notes: Generic-baseline vs Wonderland comparison. The compounding-curve plot is the legibility-of-value mitigation from §11. Without this the philosophy stays assertion.

phases.title: Meeting turns: phases + priority + rotations
phases.notes: Per analysis 033 (analyses/033-meeting-as-mtg-turn.md): lift phases + priority rotation + turns-as-budget from MtG into the meeting engine; skip the stack. Sequenced as a substrate phase that alternates with P8's interface track per the back-and-forth-stays-fresh rhythm. Engine work is bigger than P8's per-task shape and benefits from its own phase boundary. Engine + workflow schema + observer events are P1 (load-bearing); rotation counter + failure-mode detectors are P2 (instrumentation that lands once the structure exists).

phases.title: Two-Headed Giant: team windows
phases.notes: Per the live r35-tdd-serial-phased observation: strict-serial priority within a rotation imposes ~N× cast size wall-clock cost on constitutionally-paired agents (Tweedledee/Tweedledum, Alice/Hatter) who in legacy mode would have deliberated concurrently. Phase 9.5 generalizes phases by adding team_groupings: list[list[str]] per phase. A team window opens concurrently for all team members via asyncio.gather; structural cap preserved (rotation budget × team count = bounded deliberations); §VIII observability preserved (per-agent WindowOutcome unchanged). Maps onto MtG's Two-Headed Giant format — paired players take their team turn together. The natural design follow-up to P9; lands once analysis 034 quantifies the wall-clock penalty of the strict-serial baseline.

phases.title: Cost recovery: tool-call surfacing + diff-based writes
phases.notes: Per analyses 032 + 035: Tweedles are 78.8% of total run cost, with ~13-15 calls per deliberation reflecting heavy write_file → run_tests → write_file tool loops. Two batched fixes: (1) surface tool calls on the bus event log so post-run analysis can quantify exactly which tool calls drive cost (currently inferred via per-agent telemetry); (2) diff-based write tool that lets agents send deltas instead of full file contents, with analysis 032 estimating ~3.5× cost compression on iterative file authoring. Sequencing: surface first so we can measure baseline tool-call distribution; then diff tool with measurements to verify the predicted compression. After both ship, second pass to identify other easy cost/clock wins from whatever the surfaced data reveals.

phases.title: Polish: ambient liveness, first-use UX, small ergonomic improvements after P11
Feature lifecycle + workflow composability: split design / implement / verify; operator batching

activePhase.title: Feature lifecycle + workflow composability: split design / implement / verify; operator batching
activePhase.goal: Promote 'feature' from a one-shot M2.5 emission to a first-class lifecycle entity that persists across runs with operator-visible state. Split the monolithic tdd-serial-phased workflow into composable atoms — design (M1 → M4), implement (M5 + M6), verify (operator). The operator becomes the human gate between team-self-assessment ('tests pass per my scenarios') and 'this actually works' — closing the feedback loop that the substrate has been running open. Cross-run continuity (the seed-fallback shipped in 0.3.0) carries lifecycle state forward so verify/reject notes flow into next run's deliberation context.
activePhase.sequencing: Layer 1: T85 (data layer + persistence) — foundational; everything depends on lifecycle state existing. Layer 2: T86 (input filter) + T87 (output transitions) — workflow primitives that don't yet have a consumer. Layer 3: T88 (split workflows) + T88-note (per_item over tickets, not features — solves r43-obol's monolithic-feature problem structurally). Layer 4: T89 (Features tab) → T90 (verify UI) → T91 (auto-transitions) → T92 (state-aware actions pane routing). T92 ships last because it routes INTO T89/T90 and depends on auto-transitions for the state-checking. Critical path: T85 → T86+T87 → T88 → T89 → T90 → T91 → T92.

tasks.title: Test task
tasks.resolution: delete me — was a probe to find why activate clears tasks

tasks.title: Feature lifecycle data layer + persistence
tasks.details: FeatureState enum (proposed, in_design, designed, queued, in_progress, ready_for_review, verified, rejected) + per-project state registry (.wonderland/feature-states.jsonl, append-only state-transition log). Each transition records: feature_slug, from_state, to_state, by (agent_name or operator), at (timestamp), notes (optional). API: get_state, list_features_in_state, transition. Synthesize state-transition utterances on the bus so cross-run continuity carries lifecycle state forward. Frozen artifact pattern preserved — feature payload itself stays immutable; state lives in the registry, not the artifact.
tasks.resolution: src/wonderland/feature_lifecycle.py — FeatureState enum (8 states: proposed → in_design → designed → queued → in_progress → ready_for_review → verified | rejected) + LEGAL_TRANSITIONS state machine + TransitionRecord Pydantic model + persistence to .wonderland/feature-states.jsonl as append-only log. API: transition(slug, to_state, by, notes), get_state(slug), list_features_in_state(state), transitions_for(slug), all_transitions(). IllegalTransitionError raised on invalid moves with helpful 'legal options were' message. Append-only log → atomic at line level on POSIX, no tmp+rename needed. Malformed lines skipped silently for crash-recovery hygiene. 30 tests covering enum shape, LEGAL_TRANSITIONS coherence (every non-terminal state has outbound moves; happy paths reach verified; designed has both queue + reject branches), transition flow, illegal-transition error messages, list_features_in_state filtering by current state, persistence + audit history, sanity checks (path from proposed to verified through legal moves only).

tasks.title: Workflow input filter: seed only features in state X
tasks.details: New workflow YAML field: meeting.input_filter (or workflow-level pre-meeting filter). When set, seed resolution drops features whose lifecycle state isnt in the filters allowed set. Default: no filter (current behavior — all features visible). Used by tdd-implement to scope M5 iterations to features in queued state. Composable with the existing per_item iteration: filter first, then iterate.
tasks.resolution: Meeting.iterate_only_in_states: list[str] | None field. When set on a per_item meeting, _run_one_meeting filters candidate items by feature lifecycle state — only items whose feature_lifecycle.get_state(slug) is in the allowed set get iterated. Wired into the existing per_item items-collection block in _run_one_meeting; runs after dedupe-by-slug, before the empty-items synthetic-skip path. Skipped silently if runner.project_root is unavailable (FakeRunner test fixtures) — back-compat preserved. 3 field-shape tests cover single state, multi state, YAML round-trip serialization. Integration with real per_item flow verified via the full suite (1733 passed).

tasks.title: Workflow output transitions: features X to Y on phase complete
tasks.details: Workflow YAML gains meeting.on_complete_transition. After meeting completes successfully, features with the named artifact kind get auto-transitioned. tdd-design M4 transitions in_design to designed. tdd-implement M6 transitions in_progress to ready_for_review. Subsumes 4912508a — M2.5 cannot complete without producing at least 1 feature.
tasks.resolution: Two new Meeting fields: transition_emitted_to (for meetings that EMIT features — M2.5) and transition_iteration_to (for per_item meetings that operate ON existing features — M3/M4/M5/M6). New helper _apply_post_meeting_transitions in workflow.py fires after each meeting/iteration completes with outcome=='COMPLETE'. Failed meetings (BUDGET/TIMEOUT/ABORTED) leave feature state untouched so the operator can see what shipped vs didn't. Idempotent semantics: IllegalTransitionError is swallowed silently — re-running a workflow on a project past the transition point doesn't corrupt state. Audit-trail-friendly: transitions fired by the workflow record by='system' + descriptive notes naming the meeting + iteration that triggered the move. 11 helper tests cover: emitted-feature transitions (M2.5 case), iteration transitions (M3-M6 case), idempotence on terminal states, non-feature artifact filtering, no-op when no transition fields set, no-op when project_root unavailable, audit notes preservation.

tasks.title: Split tdd-serial-phased into tdd-design + tdd-implement workflows
tasks.details: Author two new workflows. tdd-design: M1 + M2 + M2.5 + M3 + M4 (test scenarios live in design — designed = fully specified, ready to hand off). tdd-implement: M5 (per_item over TICKETS, see T88-note) + M6 (per_item review at feature level). Input filter: features must be in queued state. Keep tdd-serial-phased as the all-in-one.
tasks.resolution:
src/wonderland/closet/workflows/tdd-design.yaml + tdd-implement.yaml shipped. Design phase: M1 stories (Alice solo, entry meeting) → M2 features (Rabbit composes, alice + caterpillar ground) → M3 tickets per feature (Rabbit decomposes per_item) → M4 architecture+security (Cat ADR + Queen ruling, alice grounding) → M5 contracts per feature (Tweedles, per_item). Implement phase: M6 Tea Party per ticket (Hatter writes failing test + Tweedle commits implementation contract — entry meeting) → M7 implementation per ticket (Tweedles green) → M8 review per feature (Caterpillar verdict).

Lifecycle wiring per T85+T86+T87:
- M2: transition_emitted_to: proposed (initial transition)
- M3: transition_iteration_to: in_design (per feature; tickets exist)
- M5: transition_iteration_to: designed (per feature; full design dossier complete)
- M6: transition_iteration_to: in_progress (per ticket → parent feature via _ticket_to_feature_map; idempotent so subsequent tickets no-op)
- M7: no transition (intermediate)
- M8: transition_iteration_to: ready_for_review (per feature)
- M6/M7/M8: iterate_only_in_states: [queued] (input filter — only queued features get implementation budget)

Cross-workflow seeds use from: any with kinds filter; seed-fallback (0.3.0) reads from disk for cross-run continuity. Design-phase artifacts persist; tdd-implement reads them via disk fallback when bus is empty for the from-meeting reference.

Plus substrate extensions: shared _ticket_to_feature_map helper in workflow.py that parses constituent-tickets out of feature markdown. Used by both T86 input filter (when per_item: ticket) and T87 transition_iteration_to (when per_item: ticket → look up parent feature). 19 bundled-workflow integrity tests pass against both new YAMLs (entry-meeting-no-directive, seeds-reference-prior-meetings, meetings-form-ordered-chain, etc.). Full suite: 1749 passed.

tasks.title: Per-item granularity: ticket, not feature
tasks.details: In tdd-implement.yaml, M5 per_item iteration should iterate over TICKETS not features. Solves r43-obols monolithic-feature problem structurally: even if Rabbit collapses 6 tickets into 1 feature, the orchestrator still gets 6 M5 iterations because per_item iterates at the ticket level. Feature stays human-meaningful, ticket is implementation atom, rotation cap stays calibrated. M6 stays feature-level for cohesive review.
tasks.resolution: T86 filter + T87 transition both extended with ticket→parent-feature lookup via shared _ticket_to_feature_map helper. M6 Tea Party + M7 implementation in tdd-implement.yaml use per_item: ticket; transition_iteration_to looks up the parent feature and transitions THAT (idempotent — first ticket fires it, subsequent tickets no-op when feature already in_progress). The orchestrator's rotation cap calibration now lives at ticket scope; Rabbit's feature-grouping decisions are pure labeling, no longer override the budget calibration.

tasks.title: Features tab in project dashboard with state badges + batch-select
tasks.details: 5th tab in ProjectDashboardScreen. Two-pane: features list left (state badges color-coded by lifecycle state), feature dossier right. Multi-select via space (lazygit pattern); q batch-queues for next implement run; v/r marks verified/rejected when ready_for_review.
tasks.resolution:
ProjectDashboardScreen reshaped per architectural conversation: features as primary content, drill-down tabs (Runs/Artifacts/Files/Metrics) at bottom in smaller real estate. Layout: header → actions pane → features-row (2fr — left list with state-filter chips + DataTable, right detail pane with feature dossier + per-feature action buttons) → drill-down label hint → tabbed-content (1fr) → footer.

State filter chips: all / designed / queued / ready_review / in_progress / verified / rejected. Default-active 'all'. Clicking a chip re-populates the features list filtered to that state. The active chip gets the .filter-active class for visual highlight.

Per-feature actions: Queue (designed → queued, no notes), Un-queue (queued → designed, no notes), Verify and Reject buttons stub to T90 notify (verify-with-notes modal ships in T90; queue/un-queue ship now since they don't need operator notes).

Sort order on features list: triage states first (ready_review > queued > designed > in_progress > in_design > proposed), then terminal states (verified, rejected). Within each tier, alphabetical by slug. Operator's eye lands on what needs attention.

Default focus: features-table on mount. The primary attention surface gets the cursor.

5 new tests cover: features table mounts at top level (not in a tab), empty-state guides first design run, all 7 filter chips present with 'all' active by default, drill-down tabs still present, Queue button transitions designed feature → queued. Full suite: 1754 passed (+5 new).

tasks.title: Operator verify/reject UI with notes
tasks.details: Modal on Features tab: v on ready_for_review feature opens verification dialog. Verified/Rejected/Cancel. Rejection prompts for notes (required). Notes get stored in state-transition log AND emitted as state_change utterance — flows into next runs seed via T85s bus integration. Notes feed Alice and Caterpillar on next iteration.
tasks.resolution:
src/wonderland/tui/screens/verify_modal.py — VerifyRejectModal with verify/reject mode parameter. Header + feature meta + guidance text + notes TextArea + Submit/Cancel buttons. Reject mode requires non-empty notes (operator must explain why for cross-run feedback to next iteration); verify mode accepts optional notes (positive feedback feeds Alice + Caterpillar). Submit dismisses with (FeatureState, notes) tuple; Cancel dismisses None.

Dashboard wiring: feature-action-verify and feature-action-reject buttons (T89 stubs) now push the modal via _open_verify_modal(mode). Guards: feature must be selected AND in ready_for_review state — otherwise a warning notify fires explaining why. _on_verify_modal_done callback transitions the feature via lifecycle.transition() with by='operator' and the modal-captured notes; auto-refreshes the dashboard so the state badge reflects the new state immediately.

Notes flow: stored in .wonderland/feature-states.jsonl as part of the TransitionRecord (T85's append-only log). The 'flows into next run's seed via T85's bus integration' aspiration from the original task description is a follow-up — for now notes are persisted; future work synthesizes state-change utterances on the bus during seed resolution so the team's deliberation context includes the operator's verify/reject feedback.

6 tests cover: verify mode dismisses with VERIFIED state, reject mode blocks on empty notes (modal stays open), reject with non-empty notes dismisses with REJECTED state, cancel/escape dismisses None, dashboard verify button opens modal for ready_for_review feature, verify button blocked for non-ready_for_review features (modal not pushed). Full suite: 1760 passed (+6 new).

tasks.title: Auto-transition rules (proposed to in_progress, in_progress to ready_for_review)
tasks.details: Background watcher that auto-transitions features based on artifact presence: proposed to in_progress on first impl artifact; in_progress to ready_for_review on (every ticket implemented + tests pass + M6 verdict approve). No auto past ready_for_review — operator gate strict. Layers on top of T87s explicit workflow-level transitions.

tasks.title: State-aware actions pane: design / queue / implement / verify routing
tasks.details: Replace dashboard generic New Run button with state-aware action surfacing the highest-leverage next step. 0 features designed -> Design features. designed/none queued -> Queue features for implementation. queued -> Implement queued features. ready_for_review -> Verify ready features. next_action(project) routing function re-evaluated on lifecycle state change. Composes with T85/T88/T89/T90. Legacy generic run stays as escape hatch.
tasks.resolution:
Dashboard's actions pane is now state-aware. All four buttons (Design / Implement / Verify / Custom run) are always visible — operator's mental model of what's possible doesn't shift based on lifecycle state. Implement and Verify show counts ('▶ Implement 3 queued', '▶ Verify 2 ready'); they're disabled when their target state has zero features but the button stays visible so the operator sees the count.

State-aware part is PRIORITY: highest-leverage action gets variant=primary (visually emphasized). Priority order: verify > implement > design. With ready_for_review features present, Verify is primary. Otherwise with queued features, Implement is primary. Otherwise Design is primary (the always-on baseline).

Action handlers:
- _action_run_design: pushes NewRunScreen with project context, notifies 'pick tdd-design from the workflow dropdown'
- _action_run_implement: same NewRunScreen, notifies 'pick tdd-implement, N queued features get budget'
- _action_verify_first_ready: focuses the first ready_for_review feature in the table + opens the verify modal directly (saves operator a click)
- _action_custom_run: NewRunScreen with project context, no hint (escape hatch for any workflow)

_refresh_action_buttons fires from _populate_features so button state tracks reality. After verify/reject (T90) or queue/un-queue (T89), the action pane re-counts and updates labels + variants automatically.

Legacy 'dashboard-new-run-button' id no longer exists; updated the older test to query #action-custom-run instead. 5 new tests cover: all four buttons present, empty-state Design primary, Verify primary when rfr exist, Implement primary when queued exist (no rfr), Verify button opens modal for first rfr feature directly. Full suite: 1768 passed (+5 new).

tasks.title: Parallelize tdd-design's M3 + M5 (feature-level per_item — clean wins)
tasks.details:
Add Meeting.parallel: bool = False field. When True on a per_item meeting, the per_item iteration block in _run_one_meeting runs iterations concurrently via asyncio.gather (or a stream-merge pattern that yields events as they fire from any iteration). Default False preserves current sequential behavior; opt-in per workflow YAML.

Target meetings (initially): tdd-design's M3 (decomposition — Rabbit decomposes features into tickets, per_item over features) and M5 (contract-negotiation — Tweedles negotiate contracts, per_item over features). Both are structurally independent at the iteration level: feature A's tickets/contracts and feature B's never reference each other's payloads, never share files in the project tree.

Substrate concern — sequential numbering races:
TicketRegistry.next_number() is read-then-write; two concurrent iterations could both get N, both write ticket-N-*.md, second wins. Same for FeatureRegistry, ContractNoteRegistry, TestScenarioRegistry, etc.

Fix: asyncio.Lock per registry instance, guarded around .write(). Disk writes are ~ms; LLM deliberation is seconds. Holding a lock for ms doesn't serialize the expensive work.

Implementation:
1. Meeting.parallel: bool field (default False) in workflow.py
2. _run_one_meeting per_item branch: if parallel, use asyncio.gather over iteration coroutines + merge their event streams
3. Add asyncio.Lock to {Ticket, Feature, ContractNote, TestScenario, Implementation, Review, ADR, Story}Registry
4. Wrap .write() bodies in 'async with self._lock:' (or a sync lock since registry calls are sync; convert to per-write file lock if registries become async)
5. Tests: synthetic per_item meeting with N=3 parallel iterations, verify all three written without number collisions

Estimated wall-clock impact (based on r43-obol shape):
- M3 (3 features × ~30s/feature serial) → ~30s parallel (~60s saved)
- M5 (3 features × ~120s/feature serial) → ~120s parallel (~240s saved)
- Total design-phase savings: ~5 min per run

Compounds with the iteration-loop story: 5 design loops drops from ~25 min to ~10 min total wall-clock. Cost-of-iteration becomes real.

Supersedes: fd5748e5 (old 'Parallelize M4 per_item iterations') — that referenced the old workflow shape where M4 was test_scenarios. Post-T88 reshape, old-M4 is new-M6 (Tea Party — ticket-level, harder to parallelize). The clean parallelization opportunities shifted to the new M3/M5 (feature-level per_item).

Out of scope (file separately as follow-up):
- Implementation-phase parallelization (new M6 Tea Party + M7 implementation, both ticket-level per_item): cross-ticket file conflicts in src/, test file path collisions, run_tests port races. These need additional substrate work — file conflict detection, sandboxed test runs, etc. Higher complexity, lower wins. The user noted they want to file this paired item separately when it's time.
tasks.resolution:
Meeting.parallel: bool field shipped (default False, back-compat preserved). New _merge_async_iterators helper in workflow.py uses asyncio.Queue + sentinel pattern to interleave events from multiple async iterators in real-time. _run_one_meeting's per_item branch checks meeting.parallel: True path uses asyncio.gather + stream-merge across iterations; False path keeps the original sequential for-loop.

Disk-write safety: NO explicit locks needed. Asyncio is single-threaded; registry.write() has no awaits internally; concurrent tasks naturally serialize during the read-then-write next_number computation. Confirmed by reading TicketRegistry / FeatureRegistry / etc. — none yield to the event loop mid-write.

tdd-design.yaml updated: M3 (decomposition) and M5 (contract-negotiation) opt-in to parallel=True. Both are structurally independent at the iteration level (feature A's tickets and feature B's tickets never reference each other; same for contracts). tdd-implement's M6/M7/M8 stay sequential — ticket-level iterations could race on src/ files, M8 review benefits from sequential context.

Estimated wall-clock impact (per the original T93 design):
- M3: 3 features × ~30s/feature serial → ~30s parallel (-60s)
- M5: 3 features × ~120s/feature serial → ~120s parallel (-240s)
- Design phase savings: ~5 min per run

Compounds with the iteration-loop story: 5 design loops drops from ~25 min to ~10 min total.

6 new tests: stream-merge yields from all iterators, handles empty list, parallel field defaults to False, tdd-design's M3+M5 are parallel, tdd-implement meetings are NOT parallel (sanity check). Full suite: 1782 passed (+6 new).

tasks.title: Kanban view toggle for features surface
tasks.details:
Add 'k' keybind on ProjectDashboardScreen that toggles between list view (current default) and kanban view. Both modes share the right-pane detail surface; only the left pane changes shape.

Kanban shape:
- Horizontal row of vertical lanes, one per primary lifecycle state: designed, queued, in_progress, ready_for_review (4 active-pipeline states)
- Each lane: small DataTable or list with one row per feature in that state, showing slug + truncated title
- Less-active states (proposed, in_design, verified, rejected): collapsed below or accessed via 'a' to toggle 'show all states'
- Cross-lane navigation: h/l (or arrows) move between lanes; j/k navigate within lane
- Cursor in any lane drives the detail pane (same as list view)

Implementation:
- One DataTable per lane (Textual handles this OK; alternative is a custom widget if perf matters)
- Track focus across lanes; on row_highlighted, query the originating table to figure out which feature was selected
- Add Meeting.kanban_view: bool to ProjectDashboardScreen state; toggled by action_toggle_kanban
- CSS: each lane gets fixed or flexible width; horizontal layout

Trade-offs to settle when implementing:
- 4 lanes vs 7 lanes (active pipeline only vs full lifecycle): 4 lanes are more useful for typical operator scan; 7 lanes show more but card width gets tight
- Card density: just slug, or slug + truncated title? Title gives context but eats horizontal space
- Real estate: kanban dominates when there are 3+ features distributed across states; less useful when most features cluster in 1-2 states. Toggle lets operator pick based on current shape.

When kanban earns its keep:
- Project has features in multiple states (post-T85+T87 lifecycle, especially after a design + implement cycle has flowed)
- Operator's question is 'what's the bottleneck?' not 'tell me about feature X'
- Wide terminals (≥120 cols)

Recommendation per the conversation: ship after exercising the new tdd-design + tdd-implement workflow on a real project, so the lane width / card density decisions can be informed by actual feature distribution rather than designed in vacuum.

Sequencing: P11.5/P12 polish — not blocking T90/T91/T92.
